The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 102, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention and sanctified are His names: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves. No! You will come to know. Then, no! You will come to know. No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty. You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty. Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss.﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Competition in the boasting of wealth and numbers diverts you, O people, from obedience to your Lord, and from what would save you from His wrath upon you.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e. the exegetes) said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾: He said: They used to say, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and we are more numerous in supporters than the sons of so-and-so." And they were falling away every day until the last of them, and by Allah, they did not cease to be so until all of them became people of the graves.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾: He said: They said, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so." This diverted them until they died in misguidance.

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) a statement which indicates that its meaning is competition in wealth.

Mention of the report to that effect:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, that he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾, and he (ﷺ) said: "Son of Adam, you have no wealth except what you eat and so consume, or what you wear and so wear out, or what you give in charity and so send forward."

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: We used to regard this hadith as part of the Qur'an: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would wish for a third valley, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whoever repents," until this surah was revealed: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ to its end. And his (ﷺ) saying after his recitation of "diverts you," "You have no wealth except such and such," indicates that the meaning of that, in his view, is: "Competition in worldly gain diverts you": wealth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾:

That is, until you go to the graves and are buried in them. In this is evidence for the correctness of the view regarding the punishment of the grave, because Allah, may His mention be exalted, informed about these people whom competition diverted, that they will come to know what they will encounter when they visit the graves, as a threat and warning from Him to them.

Ahl al-ta'wil said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Qays, from Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: We used to doubt the punishment of the grave, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ ... to ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, regarding the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ was revealed regarding the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave, until ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾ was revealed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾:

Its meaning, by His saying, may His mention be exalted, is: No! This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You will come to know﴾:

He, may His praise be exalted, says: You will come to know when you visit the graves, O you whom competition has diverted, the consequence of your action and your preoccupation with competition in this world away from obedience to Allah, your Lord.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾:

He says: Then, this is not how you should act, that competition in wealth and abundance of numbers should divert you. You will come to know, when you visit the graves, what you will encounter when you visit them, of the harm of your preoccupation with competition away from obedience to your Lord. He repeated His saying: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ twice, because when the Arabs wish to intensify a warning and threat, they repeat the word twice.

It has been related from al-Dahhak regarding this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿No! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The disbelievers." ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The believers." And thus he used to recite it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty﴾:

He, may His mention be exalted, says: This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you, O people. If only you, O people, knew with certain knowledge that Allah will resurrect you on the Day of Resurrection after your death, from your graves, competition would not have diverted you from obedience to Allah, your Lord, and you would have hastened to His worship, to conforming to His command and prohibition, and to renouncing the world out of fear for yourselves of His punishment.

Ahl al-ta'wil said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty﴾: "We used to be told that the knowledge of certainty is that one knows that Allah will resurrect him after death."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire﴾:

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this. The reciters of the metropolitan cities recited it as ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ﴾ with a fatha on the ta' in both instances, while al-Kisa'i recited it with a damma on the ta' in the first and a fatha in the second.

Our view regarding this is the fatha in both instances, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars upon it. Given that this is so, the interpretation of the speech is: You will surely see, O polytheists, Hell on the Day of Resurrection, and then you will see it directly, without being absent from it.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾: He meant: the people of polytheism.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾:

He says: Then Allah, mighty and majestic, will surely question you about the bliss you enjoyed in the world: what you did with it, from where you obtained it, on what you acquired it, and what you did with it.

The people of interpretation differed regarding what that bliss is. Some of them said: It is security and health.

Mention of those who said this:

Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: He said: Security and health.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: He said: Security and health.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: It reached me regarding His saying: ﴿You will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: He said: Security and health.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I heard al-Sha'bi say: The bliss about which one will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection is security and health.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Khalid al-Zayyat, from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, the like of it.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: He said: Security and health.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then they will surely be questioned that Day about what Allah bestowed upon them of blessings, what He granted them of hearing, sight, and bodily health.

Mention of those who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: He said: The bliss is the health of the bodies, the hearing, and the sight. He said: Allah will question the servants about how they used them, and He is more knowing of that than they are. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of those will be questioned about﴾.

Isma'il ibn Musa al-Fazari narrated to me, saying: 'Umar ibn Shakir informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: He used to say regarding His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: The hearing and the sight, and bodily health.

Others said: It is well-being.

Mention of those who said this:

Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Nuh ibn Darraj narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far, regarding ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: He said: Well-being.

Others said: Rather, it refers to some of what a person eats or drinks.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn 'Atiq, who said: I saw Sa'id ibn Jubayr being brought a cup of honey, so he drank it and said: "This is the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan ibn Bilal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ammar [[The report 176: it is the preceding hadith with the two chains before it, in meaning, but here it is mawquf (halted) upon Ibn Abi Talib. The chain to him is broken, the same as the chain of 174, because of al-Harith al-A'war and his nephew. As for those beneath them, Abu al-Mukhtar al-Ta'i and Hamzah continued in 174, and Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri and Ahmad ibn Ishaq continued in 159.]] ibn Abi 'Ammar, who said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: The Prophet (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) came to us, so we fed them dates and gave them water. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Jabir ibn al-Kurdi narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar, who said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to us, and he mentioned something similar.

al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) were sitting, the Prophet (ﷺ) came and said: "What has made you sit here?" They said: "Hunger." He said: "By the One who sent me with the truth, nothing else has brought me out." So they set out until they came to the house of a man from the Ansar. The woman met them, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Where is so-and-so?" She said: "He has gone to bring us sweet water." Then their companion came carrying his waterskin, and said: "Welcome! No visit to the servants is better than the visit I have received today." He hung his waterskin on a palm trunk, went off, and brought a bunch of dates. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick it yourself?" He said: "I wished that you would choose from it with your own eyes." Then he took a knife, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milch animal." So he slaughtered for them that day, and they ate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection: hunger drove you from your houses, and you did not return until you obtained this. This is of the bliss."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Shayban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and 'Umar: "Come along with us to Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan al-Ansari." So he took them to the shade of his orchard, spread a rug for them, then went to a palm tree and brought a cluster. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not select for us from its fresh dates?" He said: "I wanted you to choose from its fresh and its unripe dates." So they ate and drank water. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished, he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, this is of the bliss about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: this cool shade, the cool fresh dates, and cool water over them."

Salih ibn Mismar al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, saying: Shayban narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similarly, except that in his report he said: "A cool shade, cool fresh dates, and cool water."

'Ali ibn 'Isa al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hashraj ibn Nabatah, who said: Abu Basirah narrated to us, from Abu 'Asib, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by until he entered the orchard of one of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the orchard: "Feed us unripe dates." So he brought a cluster and placed it down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions ate. Then he asked for cold water and drank, and said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." 'Umar took the cluster and struck it against the ground until the unripe dates scattered, then said: "O Messenger of Allah, are we indeed going to be questioned about this?" He said: "Yes, except for a morsel with which one repels hunger, or a room in which one enters to shelter from heat and cold."

Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Hashraj ibn Nabatah, who said: Abu Basirah narrated to me, from Abu 'Asib, freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by me and called me, and I went out with him, and with him were Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). He entered an orchard belonging to one of the Ansar, and a cluster of unripe dates was brought to him from it and placed before him. He and his companions ate, then he asked for cold water and drank. Then he said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." 'Umar said: "About this on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Yes, except for three things: a cloth with which one covers one's private parts, a morsel with which one repels hunger, or a room in which one enters to shelter from heat and cold."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Juraybi, from Abu Basirah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and some of his companions ate a meal of unsifted barley bread with fatty meat, then they drank from a stream. He said: "All of this is of the bliss about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection."

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: "When ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ was revealed, he recited it until he reached ﴿You will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, about which bliss will we be questioned? It is only the two blacks: water and dates, and our swords are on our shoulders while the enemy is present!' He said: 'Indeed, that will come to be.'"

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, both saying: Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' Abu Razin al-Shami narrated to me, saying: al-Dahhak ibn 'Arzam narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing about which a servant will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection concerning bliss is that it will be said to him: 'Did We not make your body healthy for you, and quench you with cold water?'"

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: Abu Ma'mar 'Abd Allah ibn Sakhbarah said: No one in Kufa rises in the morning except in comfort. The least well-off of them in life is one who eats wheat bread, drinks the water of the Euphrates, and shades himself in shade, and that is of bliss.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi, from Thabit al-Bunani, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The bliss about which one will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: a morsel that strengthens him, water that quenches him, and a garment that covers him."

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bashshar, who said: I heard some people of Yemen say: I heard Abu Umamah say: The bliss about which one will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection is wheat bread and sweet water.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Bukayr ibn 'Atiq al-'Amiri, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "Indeed, this is the bliss about which we will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Bukayr ibn 'Atiq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "This is of the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Others said: That is everything a person enjoys in this world of anything.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 102, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "About everything of the pleasure of this world."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. (He said:) "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call every servant to account for the blessings and rights He entrusted to him."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "Indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, will call to account every possessor of blessings concerning what He bestowed upon him."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah used to say: "There are three things about which the son of Adam will not be asked, and everything beyond them is subject to questioning and reckoning, except what Allah wills: a garment with which he covers his nakedness, a morsel with which he straightens his back, and a house that shelters him."

The correct statement on this matter is: it should be said that Allah has informed us that He will question these people about the pleasure (of life). He did not specify in His report that He will question them about one kind of pleasure rather than another; rather, He made the report general concerning all of it. So He will question them about all of the pleasure, as He said, not about some of it to the exclusion of others.

End of the tafsir of Surah Alhakum (At-Takathur).

(He said:) "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call every servant to account for the blessings and rights He entrusted to him."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "Indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, will call to account every possessor of blessings concerning what He bestowed upon him."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah used to say: "There are three things about which the son of Adam will not be asked, and everything beyond them is subject to questioning and reckoning, except what Allah wills: a garment with which he covers his nakedness, a morsel with which he straightens his back, and a house that shelters him."

The correct statement on this matter is: it should be said that Allah has informed us that He will question these people about the pleasure (of life). He did not specify in His report that He will question them about one kind of pleasure rather than another; rather, He made the report general concerning all of it. So He will question them about all of the pleasure, as He said, not about some of it to the exclusion of others.

End of the tafsir of Surah Alhakum (At-Takathur).

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention and sanctified are His names: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves. No! You will come to know. Then, no! You will come to know. No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty. You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty. Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss.﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Competition in the boasting of wealth and numbers diverts you, O people, from obedience to your Lord, and from what would save you from His wrath upon you.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e. the exegetes) said what we have said about this.

And they were falling away every day until the last of them, and by Allah, they did not cease to be so until all of them became people of the graves.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾: He said: They said, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick it yourself?" He said: "I wished that you would choose from it with your own eyes." Then he took a knife, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milch animal." So he slaughtered for them that day, and they ate. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 102, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "About everything of the pleasure of this world."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. (He said:) "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call every servant to account for the blessings and rights He entrusted to him."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "Indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, will call to account every possessor of blessings concerning what He bestowed upon him."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah used to say: "There are three things about which the son of Adam will not be asked, and everything beyond them is subject to questioning and reckoning, except what Allah wills: a garment with which he covers his nakedness, a morsel with which he straightens his back, and a house that shelters him."

The correct statement on this matter is: it should be said that Allah has informed us that He will question these people about the pleasure (of life). He did not specify in His report that He will question them about one kind of pleasure rather than another; rather, He made the report general concerning all of it. So He will question them about all of the pleasure, as He said, not about some of it to the exclusion of others.

End of the tafsir of Surah Alhakum (At-Takathur).

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 102, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention and sanctified are His names: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves. No! You will come to know. Then, no! You will come to know. No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty. You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty. Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss.﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Competition in the boasting of wealth and numbers diverts you, O people, from obedience to your Lord, and from what would save you from His wrath upon you.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e. the exegetes) said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾: He said: They used to say, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and we are more numerous in supporters than the sons of so-and-so." And they were falling away every day until the last of them, and by Allah, they did not cease to be so until all of them became people of the graves.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾: He said: They said, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so." This diverted them until they died in misguidance.

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) a statement which indicates that its meaning is competition in wealth.

Mention of the report to that effect:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, that he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾, and he (ﷺ) said: "Son of Adam, you have no wealth except what you eat and so consume, or what you wear and so wear out, or what you give in charity and so send forward."

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: We used to regard this hadith as part of the Qur'an: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would wish for a third valley, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whoever repents," until this surah was revealed: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ to its end. And his (ﷺ) saying after his recitation of "diverts you," "You have no wealth except such and such," indicates that the meaning of that, in his view, is: "Competition in worldly gain diverts you": wealth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾:

That is, until you go to the graves and are buried in them. In this is evidence for the correctness of the view regarding the punishment of the grave, because Allah, may His mention be exalted, informed about these people whom competition diverted, that they will come to know what they will encounter when they visit the graves, as a threat and warning from Him to them.

Ahl al-ta'wil said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Qays, from Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: We used to doubt the punishment of the grave, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ ... to ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, regarding the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ was revealed regarding the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave, until ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾ was revealed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾:

Its meaning, by His saying, may His mention be exalted, is: No! This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You will come to know﴾:

He, may His praise be exalted, says: You will come to know when you visit the graves, O you whom competition has diverted, the consequence of your action and your preoccupation with competition in this world away from obedience to Allah, your Lord.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾:

He says: Then, this is not how you should act, that competition in wealth and abundance of numbers should divert you. You will come to know, when you visit the graves, what you will encounter when you visit them, of the harm of your preoccupation with competition away from obedience to your Lord. He repeated His saying: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ twice, because when the Arabs wish to intensify a warning and threat, they repeat the word twice.

It has been related from al-Dahhak regarding this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿No! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The disbelievers." ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The believers." And thus he used to recite it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty﴾:

He, may His mention be exalted, says: This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you, O people. If only you, O people, knew with certain knowledge that Allah will resurrect you on the Day of Resurrection after your death, from your graves, competition would not have diverted you from obedience to Allah, your Lord, and you would have hastened to His worship, to conforming to His command and prohibition, and to renouncing the world out of fear for yourselves of His punishment.

Ahl al-ta'wil said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty﴾: "We used to be told that the knowledge of certainty is that one knows that Allah will resurrect him after death."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire﴾:

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this. The reciters of the metropolitan cities recited it as ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ﴾ with a fatha on the ta' in both instances, while al-Kisa'i recited it with a damma on the ta' in the first and a fatha in the second.

Our view regarding this is the fatha in both instances, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars upon it. Given that this is so, the interpretation of the speech is: You will surely see, O polytheists, Hell on the Day of Resurrection, and then you will see it directly, without being absent from it.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾: He meant: the people of polytheism.

As for His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾:

He says: Then Allah, mighty and majestic, will surely question you about the bliss you enjoyed in the world: what you did with it, from where you obtained it, on what you acquired it, and what you did with it.

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Competition in the boasting of wealth and numbers diverts you, O people, from obedience to your Lord, and from what would save you from His wrath upon you.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e. the exegetes) said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) a statement which indicates that its meaning is competition in wealth.

Mention of the report to that effect:

And his (ﷺ) saying after his recitation of "diverts you," "You have no wealth except such and such," indicates that the meaning of that, in his view, is: "Competition in worldly gain diverts you": wealth.

As for His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾:

That is, until you go to the graves and are buried in them. In this is evidence for the correctness of the view regarding the punishment of the grave, because Allah, may His mention be exalted, informed about these people whom competition diverted, that they will come to know what they will encounter when they visit the graves, as a threat and warning from Him to them.

Ahl al-ta'wil said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Its meaning, by His saying, may His mention be exalted, is: No! This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you.

* *

He, may His praise be exalted, says: You will come to know when you visit the graves, O you whom competition has diverted, the consequence of your action and your preoccupation with competition in this world away from obedience to Allah, your Lord.

It has been related from al-Dahhak regarding this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿No! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The disbelievers." ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The believers." And thus he used to recite it.

He, may His mention be exalted, says: This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you, O people. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 102, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "About everything of the pleasure of this world."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. (He said:) "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call every servant to account for the blessings and rights He entrusted to him."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "Indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, will call to account every possessor of blessings concerning what He bestowed upon him."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah used to say: "There are three things about which the son of Adam will not be asked, and everything beyond them is subject to questioning and reckoning, except what Allah wills: a garment with which he covers his nakedness, a morsel with which he straightens his back, and a house that shelters him."

The correct statement on this matter is: it should be said that Allah has informed us that He will question these people about the pleasure (of life). He did not specify in His report that He will question them about one kind of pleasure rather than another; rather, He made the report general concerning all of it. So He will question them about all of the pleasure, as He said, not about some of it to the exclusion of others.

End of the tafsir of Surah Alhakum (At-Takathur).

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 102, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention and sanctified are His names: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves. No! You will come to know. Then, no! You will come to know. No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty. You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty. Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss.﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Competition in the boasting of wealth and numbers diverts you, O people, from obedience to your Lord, and from what would save you from His wrath upon you.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e. the exegetes) said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾: He said: They used to say, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and we are more numerous in supporters than the sons of so-and-so." And they were falling away every day until the last of them, and by Allah, they did not cease to be so until all of them became people of the graves.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾: He said: They said, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so." This diverted them until they died in misguidance.

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) a statement which indicates that its meaning is competition in wealth.

Mention of the report to that effect:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, that he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾, and he (ﷺ) said: "Son of Adam, you have no wealth except what you eat and so consume, or what you wear and so wear out, or what you give in charity and so send forward."

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: We used to regard this hadith as part of the Qur'an: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would wish for a third valley, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whoever repents," until this surah was revealed: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ to its end. And his (ﷺ) saying after his recitation of "diverts you," "You have no wealth except such and such," indicates that the meaning of that, in his view, is: "Competition in worldly gain diverts you": wealth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾:

That is, until you go to the graves and are buried in them. In this is evidence for the correctness of the view regarding the punishment of the grave, because Allah, may His mention be exalted, informed about these people whom competition diverted, that they will come to know what they will encounter when they visit the graves, as a threat and warning from Him to them.

Ahl al-ta'wil said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Qays, from Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: We used to doubt the punishment of the grave, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ ... to ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, regarding the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ was revealed regarding the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Zirr, from 'Ali, who said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave, until ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾ was revealed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾:

Its meaning, by His saying, may His mention be exalted, is: No! This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You will come to know﴾:

He, may His praise be exalted, says: You will come to know when you visit the graves, O you whom competition has diverted, the consequence of your action and your preoccupation with competition in this world away from obedience to Allah, your Lord.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾:

He says: Then, this is not how you should act, that competition in wealth and abundance of numbers should divert you. You will come to know, when you visit the graves, what you will encounter when you visit them, of the harm of your preoccupation with competition away from obedience to your Lord. He repeated His saying: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ twice, because when the Arabs wish to intensify a warning and threat, they repeat the word twice.

It has been related from al-Dahhak regarding this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿No! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The disbelievers." ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: He said: "The believers." And thus he used to recite it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty﴾:

He, may His mention be exalted, says: This is not how you should act, that competition should divert you, O people. If only you, O people, knew with certain knowledge that Allah will resurrect you on the Day of Resurrection after your death, from your graves, competition would not have diverted you from obedience to Allah, your Lord, and you would have hastened to His worship, to conforming to His command and prohibition, and to renouncing the world out of fear for yourselves of His punishment.

Ahl al-ta'wil said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty﴾: "We used to be told that the knowledge of certainty is that one knows that Allah will resurrect him after death."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire﴾:

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this. The reciters of the metropolitan cities recited it as ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ﴾ with a fatha on the ta' in both instances, while al-Kisa'i recited it with a damma on the ta' in the first and a fatha in the second.

Our view regarding this is the fatha in both instances, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars upon it. Given that this is so, the interpretation of the speech is: You will surely see, O polytheists, Hell on the Day of Resurrection, and then you will see it directly, without being absent from it.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾: He meant: the people of polytheism.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished, he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, this is of the bliss about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: this cool shade, the cool fresh dates, and cool water over them."

Salih ibn Mismar al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, saying: Shayban narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similarly, except that in his report he said: "A cool shade, cool fresh dates, and cool water."

'Ali ibn 'Isa al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hashraj ibn Nabatah, who said: Abu Basirah narrated to us, from Abu 'Asib, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by until he entered the orchard of one of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the orchard: "Feed us unripe dates." So he brought a cluster and placed it down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions ate. Then he asked for cold water and drank, and said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." 'Umar took the cluster and struck it against the ground until the unripe dates scattered, then said: "O Messenger of Allah, are we indeed going to be questioned about this?" He said: "Yes, except for a morsel with which one repels hunger, or a room in which one enters to shelter from heat and cold."

Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Hashraj ibn Nabatah, who said: Abu Basirah narrated to me, from Abu 'Asib, freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by me and called me, and I went out with him, and with him were Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). He entered an orchard belonging to one of the Ansar, and a cluster of unripe dates was brought to him from it and placed before him. He and his companions ate, then he asked for cold water and drank. Then he said: "You will surely be questioned about this on the Day of Resurrection." 'Umar said: "About this on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Yes, except for three things: a cloth with which one covers one's private parts, a morsel with which one repels hunger, or a room in which one enters to shelter from heat and cold."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Juraybi, from Abu Basirah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and some of his companions ate a meal of unsifted barley bread with fatty meat, then they drank from a stream. He said: "All of this is of the bliss about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection."

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: "When ﴿Competition in worldly gain diverts you﴾ was revealed, he recited it until he reached ﴿You will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, about which bliss will we be questioned? It is only the two blacks: water and dates, and our swords are on our shoulders while the enemy is present!' He said: 'Indeed, that will come to be.'"

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, both saying: Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' Abu Razin al-Shami narrated to me, saying: al-Dahhak ibn 'Arzam narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing about which a servant will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection concerning bliss is that it will be said to him: 'Did We not make your body healthy for you, and quench you with cold water?'"

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: Abu Ma'mar 'Abd Allah ibn Sakhbarah said: No one in Kufa rises in the morning except in comfort. The least well-off of them in life is one who eats wheat bread, drinks the water of the Euphrates, and shades himself in shade, and that is of bliss.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi, from Thabit al-Bunani, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The bliss about which one will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: a morsel that strengthens him, water that quenches him, and a garment that covers him."

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bashshar, who said: I heard some people of Yemen say: I heard Abu Umamah say: The bliss about which one will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection is wheat bread and sweet water.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Bukayr ibn 'Atiq al-'Amiri, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "Indeed, this is the bliss about which we will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Bukayr ibn 'Atiq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "This is of the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Others said: That is everything a person enjoys in this world of anything.

Mention of those who said this:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 102, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "About everything of the pleasure of this world."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. (He said:) "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call every servant to account for the blessings and rights He entrusted to him."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (of life)﴾. He said: "Indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, will call to account every possessor of blessings concerning what He bestowed upon him."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah used to say: "There are three things about which the son of Adam will not be asked, and everything beyond them is subject to questioning and reckoning, except what Allah wills: a garment with which he covers his nakedness, a morsel with which he straightens his back, and a house that shelters him."

The correct statement on this matter is: it should be said that Allah has informed us that He will question these people about the pleasure (of life). He did not specify in His report that He will question them about one kind of pleasure rather than another; rather, He made the report general concerning all of it. So He will question them about all of the pleasure, as He said, not about some of it to the exclusion of others.

End of the tafsir of Surah Alhakum (At-Takathur).
